terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, with the dative or ad
terms.gloss: come near, approach (in place or time)
evidence: Caes. BC 3.9: jamque hiems appropinquābat (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 2.6.1: cum adpropinquāre tuus adventus putārētur
terms.comment: Of places and of times: winter, a birthday, someone’s arrival.
With ad: to go right up to someone or something.

evidence: Plaut. Rud. 242: accēde ad mē atque adī contrā
terms.comment: Of going to someone, often to speak to him or ask for something.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 2.6.1: cum adpropinquāre tuus adventus putārētur

phrases.latin: deinde sēnsim atque placidē, tamquam nōscitābundus, ad hominem accēdit
phrases.english: then slowly and gently, as if recognising him, it came up to the man

phrases.latin: itaque iīs ūnctus quī accessit, pungunt
phrases.english: so if anyone comes near them wearing scent, they sting

phrases.latin: ubi es? — Ecce mē. accēde ad mē atque adī contrā.
phrases.english: where are you? — Here I am. Come up to me, come this way.

sources: Lewis & Short: appropinquo · Lewis & Short: accedo · Lewis & Short: adeo · Lewis & Short: adventus
